status: Reviewed whole-claim prerequisite necessity correction; source dispositions unchanged

edgeBefore.reason: Organising and representing data requires data, tally, frequency, and category vocabulary

edgeAfter.reason: Data, tally, frequency and category vocabulary supports precise description of organising data; the full continuous-data and chart-type repertoire is not required before sorting, counting and tabulating two or three categories.

rationale: Complete independent three-category sorting, counting, table construction/reconciliation, ordering, reading back and changed-count performance does not require mastery of the broad statistics-language inventory. Category/tally/frequency words support the task, while continuous/discrete and chart-axis/type vocabulary are separately assessable. The support link remains soft rather than an eligibility gate.

constructiveCounterexample.materials: Actual eight-card population, three categories, blank category/count table
constructiveCounterexample.independentTargetTask: Sort every card exactly once, count each category, construct correctly paired reconciling totals, order categories including ties, answer the original single-information question from the table, update a changed count and handle a neither-card without exceeding three categories.
constructiveCounterexample.completeTargetGuideRetained: Real question, raw-card sorting and tally-to-table recording, reconcile parts/whole, reading back, changed-count, other-category and tied-count cases and independent construction; no matching-only award.
constructiveCounterexample.fullPrerequisiteNotEntailed: This complete performance does not require distinguishing measured continuous variables from discrete counts, labelling bar-chart axes/scale or naming line/pie charts. Relevant category/count/tally words are supplied/taught in context; their subset does not establish the broad whole glossary.

reverseCounterexample: A pupil may accurately use discrete/continuous and chart-type vocabulary yet double-count objects, pair totals to wrong rows or fail to build/reconcile/read an independent three-category table; the claims are related but not interchangeable.
preservation: No claim/evidence/assessment/guide/age/context/standard/ID or other edge changed. Existing direct sorting/cardinality path and consumer edges remain exact. No new topic or source Full gain.
downstreamQualification: Authoring only. Review downstream scheduling/eligibility and private-state compatibility before staging/publication. No learner reset, migration or evidence reinterpretation is performed or inferred.
verification: Both complete current cards and learn/assessment guides, all four incident hard edges and two-way counterexamples read; independent semantic peer passed. No fresh guide efficacy/source-confidence flag asserted.
